_comment: Two kinds of chart entry. Events carry their date in the text (they stay true forever). Current status (allergy list, problems, active medications) is written without a date, with the date, clinician and source in metadata: the contradiction detector reads dated statements as history (an allergy in 2026 and 'none' in 2018 can both be true), so only undated status lines can contradict.

entries.text: Allergy: cephalosporins (cefalexin) - hives and lip swelling.

Encounter 2026-10-05 Northside Urgent Care (Dr. Sam Whitaker): acute sinusitis, started cefalexin 500 mg; hives and lip swelling about 2 hours after the first dose; cefalexin stopped, cetirizine given; told to avoid cephalosporins.
Triage 2026-10-05 (Jo Park, RN): lips swollen, itchy rash on the chest after his first Keflex capsule this morning.

dictation.title: Northside Urgent Care - dictated visit note, 2026-10-05
turns: Dr. Sam Whitaker (physician, Northside Urgent Care): Mr. Brandt, you were here this morning for the sinus infection and I started you on cefalexin. What happened after the first capsule?
Walter Brandt (patient): About two hours later my lips started to swell and I got an itchy rash across my chest. I have never had a reaction to anything before.
Dr. Sam Whitaker (physician, Northside Urgent Care): That is an allergic reaction to the cefalexin. We are stopping it today, and I gave you cetirizine. Your breathing and throat are fine.
Walter Brandt (patient): So I should not take that one again?

Dr. Sam Whitaker (physician, Northside Urgent Care): Not cefalexin, and not any cephalosporin antibiotic. I am recording a cephalosporin allergy. Tell any doctor who prescribes you an antibiotic, and follow up with Dr. Okafor next week about the sinusitis.
Walter Brandt (patient): I have an appointment with her on the twelfth.

visit.reason: Follow-up: sinusitis still not better after a week

semantic_question: Has Walter ever reacted badly to an antibiotic?
